title: Add rollout SLO gates for runtime 1.21 (p95/p99 + error-rate) with rollback recommendation
author: Aisha Bello
description:
Context: Runtime 1.21 includes kernel auto-selection v2, which can materially shift latency distributions (especially p99) and can surface SKU-specific regressions. We need a consistent, automated gate that turns canary metrics into a clear “promote/hold/rollback” recommendation, and that is deterministic and explainable for release oncall.

This PR adds rollout SLO gating checks to slo-toolkit, scoped to runtime 1.21 canary stages. The gate compares canary vs baseline within the same region/pool and evaluates: (1) p95 and p99 latency regression budgets, (2) request error-rate thresholds (5xx + timeouts), and (3) minimum traffic/sample-size requirements to avoid flapping decisions from sparse canaries. The gate produces a structured decision output used by Release Engineering and SRE automation to recommend rollback when thresholds are exceeded.

What’s included:
- New gate: runtime_1_21_rollout_slo_gate
  - Inputs: service=runtime-inference, stage={hosted-canary|dedicated-canary}, region, model_group (optional), metric_window.
  - Baseline selection: same region, previous stable runtime version (default: last GA build on that pool).
  - Metrics (PromQL-backed):
    - latency_p95_ms (request end-to-end)
    - latency_p99_ms (request end-to-end)
    - error_rate (5xx + timeout classified errors)
  - Regression budgets (defaults; configurable by stage):
    - p95: +3% allowed (hosted-canary), +2% (dedicated-canary)
    - p99: +5% allowed (hosted-canary), +4% (dedicated-canary)
    - error_rate: absolute +0.10% allowed OR relative +25% (whichever is tighter)
  - Sample size guardrails:
    - min_requests: 25k per window (hosted-canary) / 10k (dedicated-canary)
    - min_error_events: 30 (to avoid dividing by near-zero baselines)
  - Decision:
    - PASS: within budgets and sample-size met
    - HOLD: sample-size insufficient (explicitly not a pass)
    - FAIL: thresholds exceeded; emits rollback_recommended=true and a short explanation string

- Output artifact:
  - Writes a machine-readable JSON summary to the gate output directory (used by the release train controller).
  - Also prints a human-readable single-line summary for oncall copy/paste (ex: “FAIL p99 +9.2% > +5% budget, error_rate +0.14% abs > +0.10% budget; rollback recommended”).

- Fix for metric cardinality surprise (related to INT-10411):
  - The new queries avoid high-cardinality label sets (no per-kernel/per-model labels by default). Instead the gate evaluates aggregate request metrics keyed by pool/region, with an optional model_group dimension when explicitly requested.
  - Adds a unit test covering query rendering to prevent accidental label explosions.

Code/structure:
- Adds gate implementation in gates/runtime/runtime_1_21_rollout.py
- Adds config template gates/runtime/runtime_1_21_rollout.yaml with stage-specific budgets and overridable defaults
- Adds query helpers in metrics/promql/runtime.py to standardize latency/error rate queries (and to keep label constraints explicit)
- Adds unit tests:
  - test_runtime_1_21_gate_passes_on_small_regression
  - test_runtime_1_21_gate_fails_on_p99_regression
  - test_runtime_1_21_gate_holds_when_insufficient_traffic
  - test_query_rendering_no_high_cardinality_labels

Operational notes:
- HOLD is intentional: a canary without enough traffic shouldn’t auto-promote. Release oncall can re-run after window extension.
- Budgets are set to be slightly stricter on Dedicated (more predictable traffic + customer-visible SLAs). If we see false positives during the first canary window, we can tune budgets in config without code changes.

Rollout plan:
- Land this behind the runtime-1.21 rollout pipeline step (Release Eng wiring in a separate change).
- Use hosted-canary first, then dedicated-canary. FAIL should trigger a rollback recommendation but not auto-rollback without a human ack in week 1.

Test plan:
- Unit tests + lint.
- Local dry run with archived canary metrics snapshot (see docs in gates/runtime/runtime_1_21_rollout.md).

Risks:
- Incorrect baseline selection can cause spurious FAILs. Mitigated by requiring exact region/pool match and logging chosen baseline labels in the decision output.
- Error classification differences across environments. Mitigated by using runtime-standard error counters (timeout + 5xx) rather than HTTP-only codes.

Refs:
- Kernel auto-selection v2 epic: ENG-4821
- Runtime 1.21 release train: ENG-4827
- Rollout allow/deny gating mechanics: ENG-4826
- Alert noise/cardinality follow-up: INT-10411

conversation_highlights: Allison Grant: “Please make sure we don’t accidentally key decisions on kernel/model labels; we can’t afford cardinality blowups during rollout.”
Aisha Bello (author): “Agreed—queries default to pool/region aggregates; model_group is opt-in and tested. Added a test to assert the rendered query label set.”
Connor O'Brien: “HOLD needs to be explicit in the output so the release controller doesn’t treat it as PASS.”
Aisha Bello (author): “Updated decision schema to include decision=HOLD + reason=insufficient_traffic, and set rollback_recommended=false for HOLD.”
Omar El-Sayed: “For error budgets, can we do absolute AND relative thresholds? Absolute for low-error baselines, relative for noisy windows.”
Aisha Bello (author): “Implemented ‘tighter-of’ logic (min of absolute delta cap and relative delta cap) and documented it in the gate output.”
Jordan Lee: “Determinism: baseline resolution must be stable given the same inputs; no ‘latest’ ambiguity.”

Aisha Bello (author): “Baseline is resolved by explicit build label from the rollout pipeline when available; otherwise last_ga tag for that pool. The chosen baseline is printed into the output for replay.”

includes explicit HOLD behavior for insufficient traffic and a rollback recommendation flag on FAIL
